objective: Turn this program's own integration history -- every badf-git work package was integrated through the tools it was building -- into committed, recomputed shadow evidence. examples/git-shadow-evidence.json lists every case with the verdict the tool renders: the 4 record-bearing landings (landed content tree == expected_content_tree), the 11 landings without a record (composition_verified: false, honestly), the 14 identity-conforming first-parent landings, the SOURCE_ADVANCED staleness case between the GIT-F and GIT-G landings, the RELEASE_BOUND baseline, and the CI runner citations; tests/test_badf_git_shadow.py recomputes every case from the object store with the real tools (content_tree on each landing, the identity rule on each squash, git_staleness in a scratch clone, git_release_check) and refuses a tampered record or a case that cannot be recomputed offline. evidence/shadow-evidence.md carries the measurement table, the declared non-coverage (rewrite verdicts synthetic-only; recovery on real dirty state observed not committed; branch-name conformance API-observed; tag signing absent) and why the root stays DESIGNED: advancing the family is the operator's admission decision (GIT-J). No registry status change, no lifecycle change, no new control, no new tool.
business_value: SHADOWED means the controls were run against real cases and behaved. badf-git's synthetic proofs are strong, but the strongest evidence is the history that actually happened: rebases under a moving main, stale claims refused and recomputed, landings verified. Recording it once and recomputing it on every run makes the admission decision (GIT-J) rest on measured history that cannot drift -- GTGM v0.1 section 17 (GIT-I).
